draft.title: Turning points of the war
card: In June 1942, United States naval forces defeated Japan at the Battle of Midway in the Pacific. Japan lost four aircraft carriers, and its advance was stopped.
From 1942 to early 1943, Soviet forces fought German troops in the city of Stalingrad. The Germans surrendered in February 1943, and Germany's advance into the Soviet Union ended.
On 6 June 1944, Allied forces landed on the beaches of Normandy in France. This opened a second front in western Europe, so Germany had to fight on two sides.
These are called turning points because after them the Allies were mostly attacking rather than defending.
draft.remember: Midway and Stalingrad stopped the advances of Japan and Germany, and D-Day opened a second front in the west.

a.q: What did the D-Day landings of 1944 achieve?
opts: They opened a second front against Germany in the west
They stopped Japan's advance across the Pacific
They ended the German attack on Stalingrad
They forced Germany to surrender within days
a.why: The landings in Normandy created a second front in western Europe, so Germany faced enemies on two sides. Midway, not D-Day, stopped Japan. Germany did not surrender until 1945.
a.clue: The landings took place in France.

b.q: Which pair correctly matches a battle with the advance it stopped?
opts: Midway stopped Japan, and Stalingrad stopped Germany
Midway stopped Germany, and Stalingrad stopped Japan
Midway and Stalingrad both stopped Japan
Midway and Stalingrad both stopped Germany
b.why: Midway was a naval battle in the Pacific against Japan. Stalingrad was fought on the Eastern Front between Soviet and German forces. Mixing up the two places gives the tempting wrong pair.
b.clue: One battle was in the Pacific and the other in the Soviet Union.

a.best: They opened a second front against Germany in the west

b.best: Midway stopped Japan, and Stalingrad stopped Germany

check.summary: No problems found. The dates and outcomes for Midway, Stalingrad and D-Day are correct, and each question has one clearly right answer that matches the card and the explanations.
